title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards for API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also indexes the most relevant architectural decision records (ADRs) and describes the review/change process for standards. The goal is to provide a single, opinionated reference for teams building production inference services and related platform components.

Scope:
- Applies to all services in the Redwood API surface, Dedicated control-plane, and Private deployments.
- Covers REST/HTTP APIs, SDK-facing contracts, internal service-to-service protocols, IaC patterns, model packaging/serving, telemetry conventions, SLOs, and ADR governance.

Principles (short):
1) Stability for consumers: contract compatibility and explicit versioning.
2) Observable by default: metrics/traces/logs must exist before launch.
3) Performance-aware by design: consider batching, KV caching, and quantization early.
4) Infrastructure as code: reproducible, auditable deployments.
5) Security & least privilege across all environments.

1) API standards
- Endpoint design & naming:
  - Use resource-oriented paths: /v{major}/{resource}/{id} for public endpoints. Example: /v1/models/{model_id}/infer.
  - Keep verbs in HTTP methods only (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE). Avoid verbs in path names.
  - Micro-versioning: major version in path (v1) for breaking changes; minor changes should be additive and documented in release notes.

- Versioning policy:
  - Major (breaking) changes: bump path version (vN) and maintain previous major for at least 90 days or until migration plan completes.
  - Deprecation: announce 30 days before disabling in non-enterprise; enterprise customers get custom timelines per contract.

- Authentication & Authorization:
  - All public and internal APIs must use mutual TLS for service-to-service; public APIs use bearer tokens (OAuth2/JWT).
  - Required headers: Authorization, X-Request-Id (opaque client-generated UUID), X-Region (when relevant).

- Error handling & standard responses:
  - Use problem+json (RFC 7807) shape for errors. Always include code, message, request_id, and retryable boolean when relevant.
  - Common status codes: 200 (OK), 202 (Accepted for async), 400 (BadRequest), 401 (Unauthorized), 403 (Forbidden), 404 (NotFound), 409 (Conflict), 429 (TooManyRequests), 500 (ServerError).

- Rate limiting & quotas:
  - Default throttle: 100 requests/minute per API key for free/hosted tier (example baseline). Dedicated/reserved customers will have configurable quotas based on contract.
  - Implement 429 with Retry-After header and transparent billing signals for client SDKs.

- API schema & documentation:
  - All public endpoints must have an OpenAPI v3 spec stored alongside service code (openapi.yaml) and published to the API catalog.
  - Example OpenAPI snippet:

  ```yaml
  openapi: 3.0.3
  info:
    title: Redwood Inference - Model Infer API
    version: 1.0.0
  paths:
    /v1/models/{model_id}/infer:
      post:
        summary: Run text generation
        parameters:
          - name: model_id
            in: path
            required: true
            schema:
              type: string
        requestBody:
          required: true
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/InferenceRequest'
  ```

2) Coding standards
- Language & repo layout:
  - Primary backend languages: Go (services), Python (inference bindings & eval tooling), and Rust/C++ for performance-critical runtime components.
  - Monorepo permitted for core platform services; service teams must follow folder-level OWNERS files.

- Style & linting:
  - Enforce gofmt/golangci-lint for Go, black/isort/flake8 for Python, rustfmt/clippy for Rust. CI must run linters and fail builds on new violations.

- Testing requirements:
  - Unit tests: >= 80% coverage targeted for critical service modules.
  - Integration tests: run against ephemeral staging infra in CI (using test harness).
  - Performance and regression tests: must be added for model-serving changes affecting latency or throughput.

- PR checklist (required before merge):
  1. Tests added/updated and passing in CI.
  2. Lint & format checks passed.
  3. Performance impact assessed (if applicable).
  4. OpenAPI/IDL updated (if API change).
  5. Documentation updated (owner/team README).

3) Infrastructure standards
- IaC patterns:
  - Use Terraform modules for common building blocks (networking, identity, compute pools). Store modules in terraform-modules repo.
  - Keep environment-specific variables in per-environment state and use Workspaces where supported.

- Network & security:
  - Default deny ingress; only allow required control-plane ports. Private deployments must support customer-managed VPC peering and transit gateway patterns.
  - All secrets go through KMS/HSM-backed secret manager (KMS keys per-customer for Private).

- Resource naming & tagging:
  - Tagging policy: service, team, environment, cost-center, owner_contact. Example tags: {"service":"inference", "team":"eng-serving-runtime", "env":"staging"}.

- Deployment & rollout pattern:
  - Blue/green or canary deployments required for control-plane changes with automated rollback on error budget breach.

- Example Terraform snippet (network):
  ```hcl
  module "vpc" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/terraform-modules.git//vpc"
    name   = "inference-vpc-${var.env}"
    cidr   = "10.0.0.0/16"
  }
  ```

4) Model-serving standards
- Model artifact & packaging:
  - Package model assets and metadata in a canonical bundle: model-{name}-{version}.tar.gz containing: weights.bin, config.json, tokenizer.json, quantization_profile.yaml (if used), and a manifest.json.
  - Manifest MUST include model_id, version, framework, expected_max_seq_len, recommended_quantization_profile, and checksum.

- Quantization & profiles:
  - Quantization profiles are first-class artifacts; every quantized variant must include quality regression test results and token-level throughput numbers. Store profiles under quantization-profiles/{model}/{profile}.yaml.

- Serving runtime contracts:
  - Inference API must support explicit arguments for: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stop sequences, and streaming.
  - KV cache compatibility: indicate whether model supports persistent KV cache and what granularity (token-level vs request-level).

- Rollout policy for new model versions:
  1. Internal canary (10% traffic, 24 hours) with automated quality/regression checks on pre-defined prompt sets.
  2. Gradual ramp to 50% over 48 hours if metrics pass.
  3. Full rollout after 7 days with no regressions or customer opt-out exceptions.

- Model evaluation & quality gate:
  - Every new model/version must pass a quality gate defined in applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks that includes NPS-like human evals for critical prompts and automated metrics (toxicity, factuality proxies, BLEU/ROUGE for tasks where applicable).

5) Observability standards
- Metrics (SLIs/telemetry):
  - Required metrics for any serving service: request_count, request_errors, latency_p50, latency_p95, latency_p99, tokens_generated/sec, token_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, batch_size_distribution.
  - Metric names are snake_case, prefixed with service name: example inference.latency_p95_ms. Units must be documented in metric metadata.

- Tracing & logs:
  - W3C TraceContext headers for distributed traces. Critical spans: request_receive, model_lookup, runtime_inference, postprocessing, response_send.
  - Logs: structured JSON logs with keys: timestamp, level, service, request_id, user_id (obfuscated where needed), model_id, latency_ms.

- Dashboards & alerts:
  - Each service must ship a set of standard dashboards: overview (traffic/latency/errors), SLO health, cost by model, per-route latency.
  - Alert thresholds (examples):
    - latency_p95 > 500ms for inference => SEV-2 alert.
    - error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m => SEV-2.
    - kv_cache_hit_rate < 20% drop from baseline => SEV-3 investigate degradation.

- Logging retention & privacy:
  - Default retention: 90 days for dev/staging, 365 days for production audit logs. Personal data must be redacted or hashed in logs.

6) Performance standards & benchmarking
- SLOs & SLIs (platform baseline):
  - Inference-hosted (p50): <= 80ms token initial latency for short prompts (<= 64 tokens).
  - Inference-hosted (p95): <= 350ms token latency.
  - Availability SLO: 99.9% monthly for hosted control-plane endpoints.
  - Throughput: baseline per-GPU throughput measured and published per model in model catalog.

- Benchmarking procedure:
  1. Use benchmarking harness in eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite.
  2. Run workloads across sequence length percentiles: 16, 64, 256, 1024 with 10k samples each.
  3. Measure cold-start, steady-state, and burst scenarios; publish p50/p95/p99 across permutations.
  4. For any perf regression > 10% on p95 compared to baseline, open a regression-triage issue and block rollout.

- Cost & efficiency goals:
  - Teams must include cost-per-token estimates for any model deployed to hosted or dedicated environments, and propose batching/quantization strategies to meet target cost thresholds.

7) ADRs (Architectural Decision Records)
- ADR index & governance:
  - Attach new ADRs in this directory under confluence/architecture-and-standards and include an ADR number and date. ADRs must follow the template: status, context, decision, consequences, and owner.

- Recent ADR highlights (examples):
  - ADR-2026-03: Runtime kernel selection strategy — Decided to use hybrid kernel picker based on sequence-length heuristics (owner: Suresh Menon).
  - ADR-2026-05: API versioning policy — Adopt path-major-versioning (owner: Nina Gomez).
  - ADR-2026-09: Default quantization profile naming and storage (owner: Jean Park).

- Sample ADR (summarized):
  - Title: ADR-2026-03 Kernel Picker
  - Status: accepted
  - Context: Multiple kernels have trade-offs by sequence length and hardware.
  - Decision: Implement a hybrid kernel selection mechanism in the runtime that profiles initial tokens and selects the kernel best matching observed sequence length distribution; fall back to safe kernel on mismatch.
  - Consequences: Improves steady-state throughput across varied workloads; requires additional profiling telemetry.

8) Ownership, review cadence, and change process
- Owners by area:
  - API standards: eng-developer-experience (owner: Marco Li).
  - Coding standards: eng-platform (owner: Priya Shah).
  - Infra standards: eng-infra (owner: Daniel Kim).
  - Model-serving standards: eng-serving-runtime (owner: Suresh Menon).
  - Observability: eng-platform & eng-sre (owner: Nina Gomez).
  - Performance: eng-serving-runtime (owner: Evan Brooks).

- Change process (for standards):
  1. Draft RFC in docs/standards-rfcs and notify reviewers.
  2. 2-week review period minimum; capture reviewer comments inline.
  3. If changes are non-breaking, owner may publish after reviewers sign-off. For breaking changes, create an ADR and schedule a cross-team review meeting.

- Emergency changes: Owners may push hotfix standard updates with a post-hoc RFC and must notify stakeholders within 48 hours.

Appendix: useful checklists & examples
- Pre-release checklist for model rollout:
  1. Manifest and artifact checksum verified.
  2. Quality gate from applied-ml-and-evals passed.
  3. Benchmarks published & regression check run.
  4. Observability dashboards instrumented and tests for alerts present.
  5. Canary runbook staged (contacts, rollback steps).

- Contact & escalation:
  - Primary channel: #eng-standards in Slack.
  - Pager rotation: eng-sre on-call (see oncall_and_incident_response runbook).

References & related pages:
- See applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks for quality gates.
- See eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite for benchmarking harness.
- See eng-infra/terraform-and-iac for module repository and examples.

Document maintenance: owners must review this document quarterly and update the ADR index as decisions are made.
